races.name: Proper Job Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Norman Fletcher
runners_data.note: Forced to lead from the front as the only true pace-setter in the race; has a STYLE_FIT flag indicating he is racing outside his most comfortable role as a prominent horse rather than a pure leader, so his chance of winning depends on whether dictating freely at a sustainable clip proves to his advantage rather than leaving him vulnerable late.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough at 2m and handles any ground, but form has been tailing off for the past twelve months with well-beaten efforts in recent handicaps; first-time hood fitted and retains a mark of 111. Yet to score in recent starts and must show something closer to his best of 12 months ago to justify favouritism on our figures.

runners_data.name: Roadshow
runners_data.note: A 247-day absence is the key flag here for trainer Paul Nicholls' charge, who returns from a lengthy layoff but showed smart form in Good ground earlier in his career including a win; prominent style suits this shape well if fitness levels are sufficient after such a long break.|
runners_data.comment: Back after a break of nearly eight months and below form prior to that in a higher-grade handicap; the yard has a strong recent record in this race and he handles today's distance and conditions. First-time cheekpieces fitted and the return to a longer distance could prove beneficial, but a lot to prove after such a long absence.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Won seven days ago and runs back quickly, which needs monitoring, but that win came over 18f on Good ground giving him solid recent evidence; a natural hold-up horse who will drop to the rear, though Good ground and a recent confidence-boosting win are positive factors in his favour.|
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap by seven lengths off this mark last time in a first-time tongue strap, running to his best form since going into handicaps; effective over 2m-3m and acts on good to soft and good. Only seven days since that win but the consistent profile gives confidence he will go close again.

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who has shown a tendency to finish in the vicinity of the frame on Good ground, though a string of mid-pack finishes (5-7-9-3-11) suggests he finds it hard to quicken sufficiently in these contests; ran ten days ago so should be fresh enough, but will need more pace to chase than Norman Fletcher is likely to provide.|
runners_data.comment: Faded out of the picture last time when the trip stretched stamina, a pattern that makes the extended journey here a concern; effective over a shorter range of 12-16 furlongs on a sound surface and first-time cheekpieces are fitted. Yet to score in recent starts with a bit still to prove over this distance.

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: Won most recently and is actually a genuine hold-up horse shuffled into midfield on the map only because the field contains too many rear-runners for all to occupy their natural position — the note here is that his best form comes from being delivered late, and a steady pace set by Norman Fletcher may not generate the pace differential he needs to produce his finishing effort.|
runners_data.comment: Back to his best last time, taking a handicap here by a length from a lower mark and in good form across both codes; acts on good ground over 2m and remains well treated on older form. Rises 4lb for that success, however, and the inconsistency in his overall record is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Ugo Bingo
runners_data.note: Prominent in style but winless in nine outings with trainer Joe Tizzard, and recent form reads 4-6-4-7-7; capable of tracking the leader but has not converted that position into victories, and Good ground seems a benign factor rather than a positive trigger.|
runners_data.comment: Has been dropping down the weights and, though held up and beaten 10 lengths here last time, shaped as though a more demanding test over this trip could produce a better result; acts on any ground over 2m-2m3f. Yet to score in recent starts but is a genuine threat if given the searching test he needs.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Has not run since 264 days ago and carries no headgear; another true hold-up operator pushed into a midfield mapping by the density of rear-runners in this field — her recent form features pulls-up and falls and the extended absence adds significant fitness uncertainty on return.|
runners_data.comment: Going too hard up front and emptying quickly last time, was well beaten, though had been in sound form before that; inconsistent overall and returning from a long absence of 264 days. Effective over 2m and should strip fitter for the run, but difficult to trust first time back from such a break.

runners_data.name: Linden Lane
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with four top-four finishes in her last five but yet to win — a hold-up horse whose natural position at the back of the field is congested in this race shape, meaning she may struggle to find her ideal berth; ran 11 days ago and has Good ground form, but a rider without a win on record here adds to the risk.|
runners_data.comment: Third here last time, beaten one and a quarter lengths off this mark over track and trip; a maiden who has been competitive without managing to get off the mark in recent starts. Acts on a sound surface over 2m and consistent enough to keep a place in the frame, though that first success remains elusive.

races.paceDynamic: Norman Fletcher is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will coast into an uncontested position from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop over 2m1f on Good turf at Newton Abbot. Roadshow and Ugo Bingo are the nearest rivals for early position but neither is a natural leader, meaning Norman Fletcher faces no pressure and can dictate his own rhythm throughout. The hold-up cluster of Cogital, Linden Lane, Applejack Poet, and Saint Polo will be anchored further back, while the field actually contains more prominence-seeking types than can simultaneously occupy the front end — Cogital, Linden Lane, and Applejack Poet are genuine rear-runners redistributed to midfield on the map because the shape leaves no room for all of them to settle naturally. A calm, front-set pace with a lone leader dictating from the front strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile, rewarding the horse who tracks Norman Fletcher and pounces at the last, rather than closers who will have too much ground to make up from a true hold-up berth in what is likely to be a steadily-run contest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Norman Fletcher dictates an uncontested, unhurried tempo and the hold-up horses find the gaps too small to close late.
scenarios.body: If Norman Fletcher dictates an uncontested, unhurried tempo and the hold-up horses find the gaps too small to close late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Norman Fletcher's early gallop is comfortable enough to suit him but a second-row tracker produces a well-timed challenge from two out.
scenarios.body: If Norman Fletcher's early gallop is comfortable enough to suit him but a second-row tracker produces a well-timed challenge from two out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the field concertinas, allowing a well-handicapped hold-up horse to produce a finishing burst from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow and the field concertinas, allowing a well-handicapped hold-up horse to produce a finishing burst from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Early Mistakes/Falls
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or interference disrupt the front end, scrambling positions and creating a more open, attritional finish.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or interference disrupt the front end, scrambling positions and creating a more open, attritional finish.

watchPoints.text: Norman Fletcher's jockey Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell is riding 7lbs claim at amateur level — any hesitation or jumping error from the sole pace-setter could collapse the entire race shape and leave the pace vacuum unfilled.
Roadshow's 247-day absence means fitness is unproven; if he blows up turning for home after tracking the leader, the race opens up dramatically for hold-up horses who have been waiting.

Cogital, Linden Lane, and Applejack Poet are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield by the race map — if they all try to settle further back than mapped, Newton Abbot's tight track could create a traffic problem on the final bend.

Saint Polo ran just seven days ago; monitor his jumping fluency early — a quick turnaround can leave horses flat at the hurdles, and a mistake could drop him out of contention from a hold-up position.

The amateur jockey field introduces elevated jumping error risk throughout — three or more horses carry REDISTRIBUTED flags suggesting positional congestion early, which combined with amateur riders increases the chance of interference at hurdles two and three.

races.name: Celebrate Racing Staff Week Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Keep Under Wraps
runners_data.comment: A Massaat colt with a mixed pedigree — a half-brother stayed 10 furlongs but another relative was poor at staying trips, with the dam showing ability only at sprint distances; pedigree alone gives no great confidence. Best treated with caution on debut, though the scope to improve with experience is unknown.

runners_data.name: Sudbury Hill
runners_data.comment: Gave first run away on hurdling debut, finishing a promising second beaten four and a half lengths; handles today's trip and ground and is likely to come on significantly for that experience. Yet to score, but the manner of that debut display suggests there is more to come when given a stronger ride.

runners_data.name: Affection
runners_data.comment: Multiple winner on the Flat in France over 10-12 furlongs on all-weather and good to soft; shaped as though crying out for a more demanding test on a recent stable appearance and the switch to hurdles over this trip looks a good fit. Yet to run under rules but the French Flat background suggests she could develop into a useful hurdler.

runners_data.name: Hearts To Heaven
runners_data.comment: A filly by Dragon Dancer out of an unraced dam, with her nearest relative making little impression at staying trips; pedigree gives mixed signals and she is best watched on debut rather than trusted. Could run creditably but is an unknown quantity first time out.

races.name: Happy Birthday June O'Dwyer Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Coumeenoole
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's seven-year-old has won twice in four recent outings at 2m3f-2m4f on good ground, goes well fresh (19 days), and is clearly suited by bowling along in front — though the step to 2m5½f is a slight query, the going and lack of challengers compensate.|
runners_data.comment: Won a novice hurdle with a great deal in hand last time, pulling clear by 15 lengths for a trainer in excellent current form, and could have more in hand for the new yard over staying trips; effective over 2m-4f-3m and suited by decent ground. First-time tongue strap fitted, and the question is whether today's more experienced rivals can close the gap.

runners_data.name: Outmaster
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls sends out this lightly-raced five-year-old, unbeaten in one hurdle run on good ground, with a 48-day break that often suits the yard; Freddie Gingell will likely sit a close second, and the form profile is strong enough to warrant respect despite the single run.|
runners_data.comment: Opened his account at Newton Abbot on debut by an emphatic margin and clearly has scope for further improvement for a top yard; first-time cheekpieces add a positive angle and he handles today's trip and going. Didn't face strong opposition that day, but the manner of that display suggests he is open to a significant step forward.

runners_data.name: Bacardi Blue
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by style who has run on good ground before (one placing from two), but recent form figures of 5-5-2-6 are modest and Bryan Carver has had no winners from four rides for the trainer in the last 14 days — needs a very specific scenario to become involved.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in a point and showed some signs on a modest hurdling debut, though was held comfortably last time; the step up in trip today looks likely to play to her strengths. Yet to score under rules, though, and has plenty to find against more experienced rivals.

runners_data.name: Ballinoulart
runners_data.note: Long absence (596 days, 29-day penalty) is the dominant concern for this eight-year-old; naturally races prominently off pace, but with Coumeenoole and Outmaster both ahead in the queue for that ground, the OR of 69 and the layoff combine to make this a difficult proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Third in a maiden point last time out, a step up on what had been shown before, though limited overall in that sphere; plenty to prove on a first start under rules and returning from a break in first-time hood. Yet to score and faces stiff competition from more experienced rivals.

runners_data.name: Glenary
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged as unknown style, with a warning on limited racecourse exposure; the 396-day absence (52-day penalty) and just one recorded hurdle start leave significant question marks, though James Best can claim a 3lb allowance and the good ground is not a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten four lengths in a point last time, a more encouraging display than what had come before; first-time hood fitted and the trainer has noted some minor ability from the pointing career. Still without a win and returning from a lengthy absence, so needs a significant performance to be considered a genuine factor.

runners_data.name: Keep Off The Sugar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form reads 0-0-7-P across various trips and surfaces, with zero wins from five hurdle starts; Catterick Frost's yard has no recent winners (0 from 1 in 14 days) and the horse looks exposed at this level regardless of race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Still learning the job at this course last time, green and unable to complete; nothing encouraging so far from either hurdling start and a half-sibling showed little at staying trips. First-time hood fitted but very much one for the experience.

races.paceDynamic: Coumeenoole is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with only Outmaster as a genuine rival for prominent ground, should secure a comfortable lead without serious pressure in a six-runner novice hurdle over 2m5½f on good ground. Outmaster will track closely from the front, but Coumeenoole's recent front-from-the-front form — two wins from the front in the last four — suggests a sustainable, metronomic gallop rather than a suicidal early burn. The hold-up brigade of Bacardi Blue, Glenary, and Keep Off The Sugar will be ridden into a chasing pack, likely two to three lengths adrift at halfway, with no serious pace injection expected until the home turn. This race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel prominently or make the running, dictate the fractions, and sustain the gallop into the final two hurdles — a clear advantage for the lead/prominent profile. Ballinoulart is a natural prominent racer who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because Coumeenoole and Outmaster are both genuine front-runners who will occupy that space; Coumeenoole and Outmaster are far more likely to actually secure the prominent berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coumeenoole Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Coumeenoole bowls along in front at a fair but uncontested gallop and Outmaster tracks without applying pressure.
scenarios.body: If Coumeenoole bowls along in front at a fair but uncontested gallop and Outmaster tracks without applying pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Outmaster Pounces Late In Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Outmaster settles beautifully off Coumeenoole's shoulder and produces a clean jumping round to challenge decisively from two out.
scenarios.body: If Outmaster settles beautifully off Coumeenoole's shoulder and produces a clean jumping round to challenge decisively from two out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to expose Coumeenoole and Outmaster, and a closer produces a sustained run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to expose Coumeenoole and Outmaster, and a closer produces a sustained run from the home turn.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the race order and the field becomes compressed, turning it into a scramble from two hurdles out.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors disrupt the race order and the field becomes compressed, turning it into a scramble from two hurdles out.

watchPoints.text: Coumeenoole's step up to 2m5½f is untested at this trip — watch whether Harry Skelton settles the mare through the first mile or pushes forward hard early, as any sign of over-racing on the good ground could leave her vulnerable from two out.

Outmaster is 48 days fresh and has only one hurdle run to his name — watch his jumping at the first few hurdles, as a novice error early could unsettle him and hand Coumeenoole an unassailable lead before the race develops.

Ballinoulart returns from 596 days off with a penalty; watch for signs of ring-rustiness early, particularly at the first couple of flights, as the long layoff combined with being squeezed for prominent ground makes an early error a real possibility.

Glenary's limited hurdling record means his jumping is an open book — watch how he travels through the first mile as his ceiling is genuinely unknown and a clean round at a fair pace could put him in contention despite the long absence.

The field is small enough that any horse losing its position through jumping errors from the third hurdle onwards will likely be unable to recover the gap on good ground — watch the jumping at the ditch if applicable and the downhill hurdles on the far side.

races.name: EBCS Hideout Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Marhaba The Champ
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Mrs S Leech, 20 days since last run, consistent placed form on good ground at similar trips (12/15 sim-going runs placed), but unable to win in this sphere and will need a stronger pace than Phantom Gold is likely to set to deliver a telling late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Shaped respectably on handicap debut here, beaten nine and a quarter lengths, and should come on for that experience with Flat form suggesting potential to do better at this level; effective over 2m on fast ground with first-time combination headgear fitted. Yet to score under rules but should progress.

runners_data.name: Phantom Gold
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner for J Candlish with I J Power aboard, 14 days fresh, excellent record on good ground (5/5 sim-going, 1W2P), but the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] flag flags this as racing somewhat out of role; in a field this full of hold-up types, however, an uncontested lead mitigates that concern substantially.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time off a 4lb lower mark and looked as though a more demanding test would have helped; a bumper and point background that points to staying trips and effective at 2m-plus on good. First-time hood fitted and yet to score in recent hurdles starts, but there is upside if given a searching examination.

runners_data.name: Katana
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for R Stephens, just 12 days between runs, solid recent form including a second last time out at 16f on good ground, and 11/13 sim-going record with four places suggests genuine reliability in these conditions — the most consistent closer in the field.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Worcester last time when a positive front-end ride down in trip produced a better effort, beaten three lengths; effective over 2m-2m-4f on soft and good and on a fair mark if that revival is genuine. Yet to score in recent starts but is a threat if the step forward from that outing carries into this.

runners_data.name: Privilege
runners_data.note: Prominent-running type for J L Flint, returning from a lengthy 334-day absence (311 days since fall), which is a significant concern; showed back-to-back seconds on good ground before that, and if fit enough, Charlie Price can ride from a handy position to exploit the moderate pace.
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts on turf last time, though returns from what appears to have been a long absence; effective at 2m-2m-2f on good ground and has shown promise at this level on older form, albeit unreliably. Has plenty to prove before this mark can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Chartwell Jock
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Nick Scholfield, four-year-old stepping up, 30 days since last run, three places from 13 good-ground runs and a recent third on good ground — a natural traveller from a handy position who is well-suited to a race run at a controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time having gone a little free early and then faded on the climb to the line, though had shown promise at the level on his two previous handicap hurdle starts; in-form trainer and effective at 2m on good. First-time hood may assist settling, and there is a real chance here if he builds on those placed efforts.

runners_data.name: Crab Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for S Hosie, only 11 days between runs, ⚠ tagged as fading in the finish, and a form string of 00PF-P tells a stark story — no wins or places, a fall in the line, and limited grounds for optimism regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Poor jumping and greenness contributed to a pulled-up effort at this course last time, and made next to no impression in points prior to switching to rules; plenty to prove and best watched. Hard to fancy with so little evidence of ability.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 18f on good ground for Barry T Murphy with Callum Pritchard, but is a true hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map due to redistribution; the style-fit discount (0.92) reflects that racing closer than preferred may compromise its chance, and it faces a step into an OR=80 contest.
runners_data.comment: Landed a race here last time by half a length off a lower mark, thriving when the contest was truly run at a strong gallop; effective over 2m-2m-3f on good and looks capable of further improvement given point form in the background. Rises 5lb for that success and the market will indicate whether connections believe he can defy the rise.

runners_data.name: Warfleet
runners_data.note: At OR=78, placed three times on good ground in recent starts, a genuine rear-of-field operator for J D Frost who has been redistributed to midfield here; likely to settle back regardless of the map, and will need a strong pace from Phantom Gold that the race shape makes unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Made a couple of jumping errors last time but ran to form, beaten four lengths here over today's trip on a similar mark; showed ability in bumpers and could improve for a longer trip as confidence grows. Yet to score and inconsistent, though first-time hood may sharpen the effort.

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for D P Summersby at OR=77, a natural hold-up runner appearing at midfield only through redistribution; the hg:p headgear angle is worth noting, and his sim-going record (9/14, 0W2P) suggests he runs his race but struggles to get to the front end of outcomes.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time without an obvious excuse, having been in better shape before that; effective over 2m-3f-2m-5f on any ground and an inconsistent maiden. First-time hood fitted and the prior form was more encouraging, but it is difficult to rely on until that latest effort is explained.

runners_data.name: Bowling Shane
runners_data.note: Hold-up juvenile for C Boultbee-Brooks, the hg:t (tongue-tie) flag is worth monitoring, 19 days since last run; returned to form with a recent third at 16f on good but prior form this season (800) was weak, and needs to improve significantly to feature off a modest pace.
runners_data.comment: Prone to setting too strong a pace and failing to last home, which proved the issue last time over a longer trip; effective at 12-14f on soft, good and all-weather and first-time hood fitted. Has shown promise on the Flat in the past but hurdles form has tailed off, and leaving that record behind is the minimum requirement here.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse for J Tickle, just 10 days since last run and equipped with hg:tp, showing a tidy 12/15 sim-going record with three places; however, redistribution into midfield reflects overcrowding at the rear, and his low OR (76) makes it hard to envisage him winning off a steady pace.
runners_data.comment: Had every opportunity last time at Uttoxeter and still only fifth, beaten nine lengths, with the mark now considered fair; effective over 2m-2m-3f on soft and good. Inconsistent and yet to score in recent starts — first-time cheekpieces need to unlock something that the recent evidence has not shown.

runners_data.name: Wise Counsellor
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for D Steele returning from 92 days off (46 days since a fall), hg:p, and a form string of 678 that reveals limited impact at OR=80; pushed to midfield through redistribution from his true hold-up role, a natural closer who will likely find the controlled pace insufficient to deliver a meaningful challenge.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in recent starts, finishing eighth and seventh before a distant effort that was at least partly a need-for-the-run performance; showed promise on the Flat but hurdles form has deteriorated and there is ground to make up now stepping into handicaps at this level. First-time hood may prompt a better showing, but has much to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Phantom Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner novice handicap hurdle and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure — the field is dominated by hold-up and midfield types who will not challenge for the lead. Phantom Gold can therefore dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo over 2m2½f on good ground, sitting out the front alone and rationing the gallop to suit itself. The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Makinbecon, Warfleet, Man Oh Man, Saucats and Wise Counsellor — have been pushed forward on the map only because there are too many true closers to show at the rear; in reality they will settle behind and face a stiffer task if the pace is modest. This shape strongly favours Phantom Gold and any prominent-to-midfield runner with tactical pace, because a controlled tempo set by a lone leader on good ground will reward horses that can travel into the race and quicken from a handy position, rather than those needing a true test of stamina from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Phantom Gold Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Gold bowls along in front without pressure and controls the tempo throughout, setting a measured pace that suits a prominent finisher.
scenarios.body: If Phantom Gold bowls along in front without pressure and controls the tempo throughout, setting a measured pace that suits a prominent finisher.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough that Phantom Gold's advantage is eroded on the run-in and one of the better-credentialled hold-up types delivers a late challenge.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just honest enough that Phantom Gold's advantage is eroded on the run-in and one of the better-credentialled hold-up types delivers a late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes more genuine mid-race and the race develops into an attritional contest that rewards stamina and jumping accuracy.
scenarios.body: If the pace becomes more genuine mid-race and the race develops into an attritional contest that rewards stamina and jumping accuracy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce from Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a surprisingly strong gallop and the field is well-strung-out, enabling true hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: If the race is run at a surprisingly strong gallop and the field is well-strung-out, enabling true hold-up horses to close.

watchPoints.text: Phantom Gold's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the race's defining factor — watch whether I J Power sends him clear immediately or settles in a rhythm; if unchallenged after the first two hurdles, the race shape crystallises firmly around SCENARIO_A.

Privilege is returning from 334 days absent (including a fall) — watch the paddock and early running for any sign of rustiness; if visibly not right, it loses its claim as a prominent challenger and SCENARIO_A narrows further.

Chartwell Jock's jumping must be monitored closely — a four-year-old in a 12-runner hurdle, any errors at the hurdles will immediately destroy its chance of sitting close enough to the pace to exploit the modest tempo.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Makinbecon, Warfleet, Man Oh Man, Saucats, Wise Counsellor — are unlikely to secure their natural rear position in a slow-tempo race; watch how many end up closer than expected in the early stages, which could ironically create more of a contest than the map suggests.

Katana's jockey C Gethings has ridden the horse before and the recent placed form is the strongest in the hold-up group — if any closer is to challenge Phantom Gold late, watch for Katana making smooth headway after the second-last hurdle as the primary signal that SCENARIO_B is unfolding.

races.name: St. Austell Brewery Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Demoiselle Kap
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here, wearing a tongue-strap and boasting six in-the-money finishes from 15 starts on good ground; she holds a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting she may be racing slightly out of her most comfortable position, but her ability to control tempo from the front in this small field is a significant structural asset.
runners_data.comment: Well below form last time, finishing ninth after a more encouraging second on the previous start; form has tailed off recently and acts on soft and good around 2m. First-time tongue strap fitted and conditions may help, but there is something to prove after that poor latest display.

runners_data.name: Walkin Out
runners_data.note: David Pipe's nine-year-old has a superb record on good ground (7/11, 1W 6P) and his last five runs all came on Good or Good-Soft — the conditions are squarely in his favour; Sam Bowen rides and a hold-up style suits him well here, tracking into a race that may set up perfectly if the front pair tire.
runners_data.comment: Won a point by eight lengths last time, reliable and likely thrown in relative to a handicap mark here; effective over 3m on good ground and has two wins in recent starts. Our top-rated runner and, despite this being her first attempt over regulation fences, the pointing form puts her ahead of the field on merit.

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's yard is in form (1/7 over 14 days) and this horse is relentlessly consistent with five seconds and a win from his last five starts on good ground; racing prominently just off Demoiselle Kap, he is ideally positioned to pounce if the leader makes any jumping errors.
runners_data.comment: Took this race off a 4lb lower mark last year and arrives only 4lb higher after a run of close seconds, just worn down late over the longer trip last time; a front-running type who relishes making it, effective around 2m-2m-4f on soft and good with the trainer in form. Should benefit from dropping back in trip and is a clear threat to our selection.

runners_data.name: Jack's A Legend
runners_data.note: Veteran eleven-year-old with an amateur rider in Miss Imogen Mathias, and his recent record on good ground is modest (4/15, 0W 1P); he prefers a hold-up role and needs a truly searching gallop to make his late run tell — this controlled pace is unlikely to suit.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in recent starts over today's trip and conditions; pulled too hard and emptied when tried at a longer distance last time but has course and distance form and handles a wide range of ground. Effective over 2m-2m-4f and looks capable of contributing from the placed positions if settling better.

runners_data.name: Vengeance
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by inclination but displaced into a midfield mapping because of the cluster of rearward types in this field; his form string shows no wins from 15 good-ground starts and he is lightly weighted at OR 82 — his best chance depends on an unusually strong gallop that this race shape may not generate.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 23 lengths in third last time over course and distance, held up and losing ground on the testing uphill finish; effective over 2m-4f-2m-7f and first-time tongue strap fitted. A maiden without a win in recent starts, but an unexposed type over fences who could stay on for minor honours.

runners_data.name: Danny's Friend
runners_data.note: Christian Williams's seven-year-old won over 2m on good ground and the step up to 2m5f is a new query; naturally a hold-up horse but mapped to midfield given the redistribution, Jack Tudor takes the ride and the 49-day break with a fit yard (2/13 in 14 days) is worth noting, though distance stamina remains unproven.
runners_data.comment: Should come on for that run last time after a long break, finishing well beaten over course and distance; effective over 2m and could get a bit further, but the overall form is limited and the gap to the leaders substantial. Hard to fancy on current evidence.

runners_data.name: School For Scandal
runners_data.note: Two pulled-ups in recent form (the P entries) are a concern for confidence and jumping fluency over 2m5f fences; showed enough in a third at 2m3f on good ground, but at OR 79 and age eleven he needs a flawless round of jumping to feature — any fence issue likely ends his race.
runners_data.comment: Came home lame having bled last time and has twice failed to complete in recent starts; effective over 2m-7f-3m2f on good to soft and good to firm when on song. The reliability question is significant and is the dominant concern until proven otherwise.

races.paceDynamic: Demoiselle Kap is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, she should dictate at a sustainable rhythm from the front across this 2m5f Newton Abbot test on good ground. Limerick Leader and School For Scandal will push to sit prominently just off her heels, creating a compact, measured pace rather than a frantic gallop. Vengeance and Danny's Friend are true hold-up types by nature but, with three horses already committed to prominent positions, both are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than ideal — the field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can comfortably accommodate at the rear, and Walkin Out and Jack's A Legend are the pair most naturally suited to the rearward slots. This measured, front-runner-controlled shape on good ground heavily favours prominent and close-tracking profiles who can travel sweetly through the race and produce a sustained jump-by-jump challenge in the final mile — pure closers dependent on a fast-run collapse of the front are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Demoiselle Kap Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Demoiselle Kap bowls along at her own tempo and the pace never truly quickens to dislodge her.
scenarios.body: If Demoiselle Kap bowls along at her own tempo and the pace never truly quickens to dislodge her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Limerick Leader and School For Scandal apply enough pressure to Demoiselle Kap to create a genuine mid-race duel.
scenarios.body: If Limerick Leader and School For Scandal apply enough pressure to Demoiselle Kap to create a genuine mid-race duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front trio over-jump or quicken too hard up the straight and leave a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: If the front trio over-jump or quicken too hard up the straight and leave a gap for a late finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Upset
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fences produce errors, fallers, or the pace collapses entirely leaving a modest contest.
scenarios.body: If multiple fences produce errors, fallers, or the pace collapses entirely leaving a modest contest.

watchPoints.text: Demoiselle Kap controls tempo entirely unchallenged — if she is allowed to bowl along without any pressure from Limerick Leader or School For Scandal, she may prove very difficult to peg back and could win well clear.

School For Scandal's recent pulled-up runs (P finishes in the form string) raise a jumping-fluency red flag at a track with unforgiving fences — watch for an early exit that could alter the race shape dramatically.

Vengeance and Danny's Friend are both natural hold-up horses forced closer to the pace by the race shape; if either is uncomfortable racing out of role and makes a jumping error under that positional pressure, it could cause interference to others.

Walkin Out has not run for 45 days (last run flagged as a 30P prep); pipe-trained and clearly fit enough to run, but watch his jumping in the early stages as he settles from the rear — any early fence wobble from being fresh could cost him ground he cannot afford to give.

Limerick Leader's five consecutive top-two finishes on good ground mark him as the form horse of the race — if he travels smoothly in behind Demoiselle Kap without being asked a question until the final fence, he is the likeliest to accelerate past the leader.

races.name: Murray Group Gallop Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Belgarum
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two recent Good-ground wins over staying trips, including a course-relevant 19f success; tongue tie and cheekpieces fitted, 27 days fresh, trainer Tizzard in 3/11 form — the key race-shaper, but OR 106 and top weight may find it hard to dominate and win from the front over this extreme 3m2½f trip.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form stepped up in trip, a half-length second off 104 last time and only 2lb higher here; won by a length at Fontwell from a 5lb lower mark penultimate start and handles a sound surface well over staying trips. First-time cheekpieces may help, though a tendency to pull up is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Striking A Pose
runners_data.note: Dual trainer Tizzard runner whose best form is a 26f Good-ground win (1/26f/GOO), consistent placed efforts at this trip and going, and blinkers fitted — genuine hold-up specialist who thrives when a lone leader sets up a staying test, though the 28-day absence and a 10-year-old age deserve monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Took this race by two and a half lengths off a 3lb lower mark three starts back and remains well treated given older efforts; effective over 2m-3m on any ground and shaped respectably at last start despite a sizeable defeat. First-time blinkers add interest, though the most recent display was well below par.

runners_data.name: Balkardy
runners_data.note: Miss Eleanor Williams takes the ride on this 9-year-old whose recent form reads poorly (56P-U7) and who has failed to win or place in any of his last five Good-ground starts; trainer T14 record of 0/3 adds little confidence, though the extreme trip is his territory and he may outrun his current form if rivals are wasteful.
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent in recent starts, finishing seventh and unseating before another poor effort last time out — hard to trust. Does handle today's trip and conditions, and the mark has eased, but must demonstrate improved reliability over hurdles before demanding inclusion.

runners_data.name: Cinnodin
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with live Good-ground credentials (1/24f/GOO, 2/24f/GOO) and a progressive profile — naturally a deep hold-up horse, though map placement in midfield reflects the congested rear; G Sheehan rides for in-form Snowden (T14 6/13), and peak form at exactly this sort of Good-ground staying trip makes him one of the most interesting runners.
runners_data.comment: Progressing as the trip increases over hurdles, going a close second off 102 last time with only 2lb more in hand here; won by a length and a quarter at a lower mark penultimate start and acts well on good ground as a reliable stayer. First-time hood fitted and our figures put him clear at the head of the market.

runners_data.name: Jafimgoso
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this Dan Skelton-trained 7-year-old (T14 11/23, a powerful combination) who has won twice on Good ground and placed four further times at similar distances — held up in his races naturally, but the map pushes him closer than ideal, meaning he must settle in a position that doesn't entirely suit if he's to produce his best.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time, beaten a length off 99 after travelling well but tending to lug under pressure, and steps up in trip having taken a race at Ludlow from a lower mark; the yard is in strong form and he looks capable of stepping forward now his problems have been addressed. Only 2lb higher than that last success and well treated given earlier form.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: Barry Murphy's 9-year-old has three consecutive second or third finishes over 26f on Good ground — a deep stayer whose entire profile screams "wait and pounce", yet placed in midfield here due to the glut of hold-up horses; James Bowen is a capable jockey, and the course-relevant distance form is genuinely strong.
runners_data.comment: Third and second in the last two starts, holding up and staying on without threatening at Cartmel last time, shaping as though an even longer test would be welcome; on a fair mark and the course and distance suit. Yet to score in recent starts and needs the pieces to fall right in behind the pace.

runners_data.name: Jager Time
runners_data.note: Fern O'Brien rides for her father's yard (T14 3/26, quiet), this 7-year-old having won a 25f Good-ground hurdle and placed in four of his last five on similar surfaces — sits naturally in the hold-up group but is shown in midfield given the field's shape, and a return to form after a recent off-pace run would be needed to figure.
runners_data.comment: Third beaten two lengths off a 1lb lower mark last time and handles this sort of trip well on good ground; effective out to 3m-plus and connections probably feel a little more is to come. Ranked last of eight on our figures, though, and has not shown enough to demand serious respect.

runners_data.name: Final Entry
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 5-year-old is the youngest and lowest-rated runner in the field, returning just 11 days after his last run (3/26f/GOO, his best recent effort) with tongue tie and visor fitted; a true hold-up performer shifted toward midfield on the map, he lacks experience at this extreme trip and the redistribution further compromises his natural style.
runners_data.comment: Third here last time out, beaten four and a half lengths after being allowed an easy lead early and then finding plenty under pressure; in decent form of late over 2m-3m on soft and good to soft, and a first-time visor is fitted. Yet to score in recent starts and likely needs everything to fall right.

races.paceDynamic: Belgarum is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 3m2½f hurdle and, with no genuine rival to pressure him from the front, he is set to control this race at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. The remaining seven runners are all natural hold-up types, though Cinnodin, Jafimgoso, I Am Spider Man, Jager Time, and Final Entry have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is nowhere else to place them — they cannot all sit as deep as they would wish, and some will inevitably race closer to the pace than is ideal. Striking A Pose and Balkardy are genuine sit-and-wait performers who will look to time their challenges from well off the pace. With one man making a controlled tempo over a long trip on Good turf, this race shape strongly favours horses who are comfortable tracking a lone leader at a genuine three-mile-plus gallop and have the jumping fluency and stamina to close late — patient hold-up horses with a proven record at this sort of trip will be most advantaged, while those pushed out of their natural position into mid-division face an awkward compromise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belgarum Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Belgarum dictates an uncontested lead throughout and the redistributed midfield horses fail to land a meaningful challenge from their compromised positions.
scenarios.body: If Belgarum dictates an uncontested lead throughout and the redistributed midfield horses fail to land a meaningful challenge from their compromised positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Patient Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine hold-up performer tracks Belgarum's measured tempo, jumps fluently throughout, and produces a well-timed challenge from the last two flights.
scenarios.body: If a genuine hold-up performer tracks Belgarum's measured tempo, jumps fluently throughout, and produces a well-timed challenge from the last two flights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up horses — forced to race closer than ideal — settles better than expected and converts a prominent position into a winning run.
scenarios.body: If one of the redistributed hold-up horses — forced to race closer than ideal — settles better than expected and converts a prominent position into a winning run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches in the back straight and then the race turns into a grinding, stamina-sapping finish from three out.
scenarios.body: If the field bunches in the back straight and then the race turns into a grinding, stamina-sapping finish from three out.

watchPoints.text: Belgarum jumps off and establishes an uncontested lead — watch whether Cinnodin or Jafimgoso, mapped into midfield, can actually settle off a slow pace rather than being sucked closer than ideal, as their ability to switch off will decide whether the winner comes from that group or from Belgarum himself.

Striking A Pose and Balkardy are both trained by the Tizzard yard (3/9 T14 form) — monitor market moves for any stable order, as running two hold-up horses from the same yard at extreme trip could involve a degree of tactical coordination that shapes who gets the better position.

Jafimgoso is a genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield — Harry Skelton is talented enough to drop him back and ignore the map position, but if he is squeezed forward early on a small field track like Newton Abbot, he may never find his rhythm over 3m2½f, which would compromise his chance significantly.

Final Entry's 11-day turnaround for a 5-year-old over a career-longest 3m2½f trip is worth monitoring — David Pipe occasionally runs horses back quickly when conditions suit, but if fitness is marginal over this extreme distance, he could drop away from halfway and create extra room for those tracking Belgarum.

Good ground has been consistent all card at Newton Abbot — no deterioration expected, which suits horses like Cinnodin and I Am Spider Man whose Good-ground form profiles are strongest, and narrows the advantage of any runner whose record is built on softer conditions.

races.name: Thatchers Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Jetty May
runners_data.note: Won over 2m6f on Good for Paul Nicholls' yard and has solid similar-going form (6/7 runs, one win, one place); Liam Harrison takes a 7lb claim which is meaningful at the weights, and the step back up to 3m2f after a 31-day break looks well-timed for a hold-up mare who stays well.
runners_data.comment: Took a race here from a 5lb lower mark penultimate start and went below form when stepped up in trip last time on the same mark; back to a more suitable distance in first-time cheekpieces with course form to call on. Our top-rated runner and capable of making the running count if reverting to that earlier level.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Two wins and six places from 15 runs on Good ground is a standout statistical angle in this field; Nick Scholfield's yard is 1/8 in the last 14 days and Harry Reed is an accomplished claimer — a 13-day turnaround after a run at 3m2f suggests he comes here cherry-ripe as a genuine hold-up type who handles this trip and going well.
runners_data.comment: Won by two and a quarter lengths off a mark 2lb higher at Hereford earlier and has now slipped back below that winning level; effective around 3m on soft and good, with the trainer in good current form. Tends to idle in front, which is the main risk, but has the form in the book to win off this mark.

runners_data.name: Hatos
runners_data.note: Joe Tizzard has saddled three runners in the past 14 days (3/8) and this gelding has placed twice at 2m4f-plus on Good; without a win on the prevailing going his form is solid rather than outstanding, and Freddie Gingell's claim could prove a handicap positive at 3m2f.
runners_data.comment: Came down last time and had been placing consistently in the two starts before that; effective around 2m-4f on soft and good ground. A tricky sort at times, but a genuine contender if he gets round safely.

runners_data.name: Illogical Logic
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, OR 83 and taking up a prominent role that is his natural position; Christian Williams' yard is 1/15 in recent form which tempers enthusiasm, but if he bowls along uncontested his jumping record at this trip on Good (9/15, 1W 4P) gives him a genuine chance of holding on.
runners_data.comment: Landed a race over course and distance off a higher mark earlier this season but has been inconsistent since and failed to complete last time; effective over 3m on good and good to soft, returning from a short break with a first-time hood. Must prove willingness to complete before placing any confidence here.

runners_data.name: Honey I'm Good
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse with 9/15 similar-going form for the Williams yard; because the field is stacked with closers, she is unlikely to get her natural rear-rank position and will instead find herself racing in midfield territory, which does not play to her strengths — a 71-day absence and the tongue tie add uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Held up and a well-beaten third at Fakenham most recently, never getting competitive over a trip she handles; better over fences than hurdles and comes here after a short break. Plenty to find in recent form but the switch back to chasing could bring about an upturn.

runners_data.name: Bucks Dream
runners_data.note: Has placed at 3m on Good (3/24f/GOO in recent history) and is a genuine hold-up type, but comes here 106 days since his last run (including a pulled-up effort); the map places him in midfield due to surplus closers in the field, meaning he may never settle into his ideal rhythm — Sheila Lewis has no entries in the 14-day trainer form column.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in a point beaten a length last time and has placed twice in recent form; first-time cheekpieces fitted and handles today's ground. Yet to score and has had jumping-related issues previously, though the balance of evidence suggests an each-way type if things go smoothly.

runners_data.name: Unspeakable
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor — one of the most in-form jump jockeys in the south — is the key angle here; an OR 80 prominent racer with two wins from 15 runs on Good, he could be the one to press Illogical Logic from the front and capitalise if the sole leader weakens from the last, though his recent string of mid-division finishes (6276-4) suggests he needs things to go right.
runners_data.comment: Drifted up the hill and struggled for fluency when fourth last time at a course that places a premium on clean jumping; effective over 3m-3m2f on a sound surface and first-time cheekpieces fitted. Unreliable and yet to score in recent starts — hard to fancy until consistency improves.

runners_data.name: Testflight
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — placed in ten of 15 runs on Good ground — and Tabitha Worsley's conditional claim is useful at the weights; at OR 76 with a string of thirds and fourths, this 9yo mare is the model of a reliable place-getter at 3m2f on Good who needs others to make mistakes to actually win.
runners_data.comment: Made a series of jumping errors last time and was clearly not at his best, a well-beaten third over course and distance; suits 3m on good ground but that display was well short of what would be needed. Needs significantly improved jumping to figure.

runners_data.name: Benny Baloo
runners_data.note: Absent for 123 days and with only 3/14 runs on similar going to show for his career, this 9yo's best form has come at 3m4f on Soft; the map shows him in midfield only because he is one of three true hold-up types who cannot all get to the rear — his natural instinct is to drop out, and that may be unworkable in a small-field, steady-pace race.
runners_data.comment: The ground may have contributed to a distant fourth last time but has been underperforming for the new yard across several recent efforts; effective over 3m-plus and has slipped down the weights. Returning from a long break and the form needs to be taken on trust — hard to be confident until it arrives.

races.paceDynamic: Illogical Logic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 3m2f handicap chase over Newton Abbot's testing Good ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Christian Williams' gelding should be able to control tempo from the front without being pressured into a punishing gallop. At 3m2f on Good ground, a lone leader setting a sustainable pace typically produces a strongly-run affair in time terms but without the frantic early burn that burns off hold-up horses — the race is likely to develop steadily before the tempo lifts from three out, playing into the hands of hold-up horses with class and jumping accuracy. Unspeakable and Testflight are the main prominent types who will shadow Illogical Logic through the early stages, but neither is sharp enough to force a brutal pace, meaning the middle portion of the race should remain within range of the closers. This shape decisively favours hold-up horses with proven form on Good ground who can travel within themselves and pick up in the final half-mile — Edgewell, Jetty May and Hatos all profile for this scenario. Three runners — Honey I'm Good, Bucks Dream and Benny Baloo — are genuine hold-up types whose natural rear-rank position has been displaced to midfield on the map because this field contains more true closers than the race shape can accommodate behind the pace; of these, Honey I'm Good is most likely to actually secure a midfield berth given her course-going profile, while Bucks Dream and Benny Baloo may struggle to achieve even that from their natural starting instincts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates Home
scenarios.trigger: If Illogical Logic is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the field's hold-up horses find insufficient injection of pace to pounce late.
scenarios.body: If Illogical Logic is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the field's hold-up horses find insufficient injection of pace to pounce late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively honest enough that the genuine hold-up horses can travel smoothly and pick off the leader from the third-last fence.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves deceptively honest enough that the genuine hold-up horses can travel smoothly and pick off the leader from the third-last fence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Unspeakable tracks Illogical Logic closely enough throughout and the pace quickens from four out to burn off the hold-up horses before they can get competitive.
scenarios.body: If Unspeakable tracks Illogical Logic closely enough throughout and the pace quickens from four out to burn off the hold-up horses before they can get competitive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsiders Capitalise On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the frontrunners and the race is run in an atypical stop-start pattern that scrambles the form book.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the frontrunners and the race is run in an atypical stop-start pattern that scrambles the form book.

watchPoints.text: Illogical Logic is the only horse with the profile and intent to lead — if he jumps cleanly at the first two fences and establishes a clear advantage, the race is effectively his to lose given the absence of any pace rival.

Honey I'm Good, Bucks Dream and Benny Baloo are all natural hold-up horses compressed into midfield by the race shape — watch whether any of them tries to drift back to their true position early on, which could cause crowding and interference with Edgewell or Hatos as they seek to settle.
Edgewell's 13-day turnaround is short for a three-mile-plus chaser — watch the pre-race market move; if he drifts from his morning price there may be a fitness concern not visible in the public form.

Jack Tudor aboard Unspeakable is worth monitoring for an aggressive front-two move after the second last — Tudor's style tends toward bold jumping rides and he may attempt to rattle up the pace from four out to burn off the hold-up horses before they get competitive.

The going is consistently Good across all seven Newton Abbot races tonight, confirming no hidden soft patches — horses with CONCERN flags on Good ground have no mitigation here, and any runner who has underperformed on this surface previously should be marked down accordingly.
